description: Field D* plans paths over a grid in which each cell has its own traversal cost, and it repairs a path when cells change. Its nodes are the cell corners, but a path may leave a corner through any point on the edge between two neighbouring corners, so it crosses cells at any angle, not only in 45-degree steps. The cost-to-goal `g` along such an edge is taken as linear between the values of its two corners (*interpolation*), and a closed form gives the best crossing point. Like D* Lite, it searches from the goal: the start can move, and after a cell changes only the affected corners are repaired. The crate returns the extracted interpolated path, or the cheapest 8-connected corner path where that one is cheaper, so the result never costs more than the 8-connected optimum.

papers.title: The Field D* Algorithm for Improved Path Planning and Replanning in Uniform and Non-Uniform Cost Environments
papers.venue: Technical report CMU-RI-TR-05-19, Robotics Institute, Carnegie Mellon University

papers.title: Using interpolation to improve path planning: The Field D* algorithm
